critiques.assumption: Removing full workshop assembly releases useful time without losing a necessary fit-and-completeness check.
critiques.limitation: D2-O2 does not separate activities; D2-O5 records insertion retries. Neither establishes that replacement fit checks are cheaper or equally effective. Forbidding full assembly is a strategy choice, not a case constraint.
critiques.opening: Retain assembly while testing the mapped-kit information mechanism, then isolate the additional effect of removing assembly.
critiques.comparison: A linked assembled organizer may deliver the identity-transfer benefit with less customer insertion burden, but retains workshop insertion time.
critiques.probe: Compare linked assembled and linked unassembled samples with identical parts, diagrams and independent final inventories; include every replacement check in workshop time.

critiques.assumption: Order-specific completeness and placement representations are correct and remain aligned.
critiques.limitation: A wrong order-to-parts mapping can make a filled card and matching diagram agree while the delivered arrangement is wrong. Supplied observations do not measure this dependency.
critiques.opening: Check mapping against the accepted order independently before evaluating the interface.
critiques.comparison: Linking tray and diagram may reduce reconciliation, but also couples their errors; neither parent alone establishes mapping accuracy.
critiques.probe: Independently derive required counts, color and positions from accepted orders and compare them with proposed maps.

openings.claim: An order-linked tray and placement diagram may improve both workshop checking and customer arrangement while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Give each tray position a corresponding diagram identifier; preserve workshop assembly and use the linked information during final checking and unpacking.
openings.prediction: Beyond Z1, the diagram should improve placement; beyond Z2, the tray should reduce selection/checking errors. Their proposed interaction is reuse of one component identity across packing and unpacking. Against A1, customer insertion burden should decrease while workshop insertion remains. Incorrect maps or labels losing their referent break this interaction.
openings.probe: Within 15 samples, allocate three each to incumbent, Z1, Z2, linked assembled and A1; cover all compartment counts and include rare color. Time all preparation/checking stages. Use ten participants in five matched-layout pairs comparing the linked assembled and A1 versions, without prior practice. These proposed diagnostics cannot establish pilot success rates.
assumptions: Mapping and identifiers remain interpretable after packing.
Footprint, assortment capacity, removable partitions, ordered counts and color remain intact.
Preparation, labels and trials fit 500 initially, 0.40 recurring and the fixed delivery date; feasibility is unmeasured.
